units.text: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network. It helps people load a site faster by delivering content from locations closer to them. We call those edge locations. The origin is where the original content lives. In this example, the store keeps its product photos in Amazon S3, a service that stores files as objects. Here is what happens when a customer requests a photo.

If the edge already has a usable copy, CloudFront sends it back right away. That is a cache hit. On a cache miss, CloudFront checks upstream and fetches the photo from S3 if needed. It returns the photo, and can keep a copy for later requests. S3 still holds the original. Use CloudFront to deliver content closer to customers. Decide separately who can reach the origin directly.
